text:
incident-bot: P0: elevated 5xx + OOMs in serving runtime across us-east-1. Autoscaler showing repeated scale-up then immediate scale-down cycles -> node churn. Paging oncall @maria :rotating_light:

maria: seeing repeated CUDA OOMs in logs, containers restarting rapidly. Metrics: pod restart count spike, node eviction events. running the runbook now.

sam: linked logs (snippet):
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] runtime: kv_cache alloc failed: CUDA out of memory
[2026-03-15T14:02:12Z] containerd: killing container serving-abc-xyz (OOMKilled)
[2026-03-15T14:02:13Z] kubelet: eviction: memory.available
```

maria: autoscaler metrics look like this: rapid replica increase from 20 -> 60 in 3m then drop to 18 in 2m repeatedly. suspect scale-policy hysteresis issue + cold-start memory pressure.

jordan: confirms. autoscaler config `scale-target: serving-cluster`, `stabilizationWindow: 0s` (bad). There's also a burst policy enabled for bursty traffic which spikes.

talia: customer tier: several enterprise customers are reporting increased latency and timeouts, some 504s. Support queue getting tickets.

maria: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) pause autoscaler, set replicas to a conservative fixed target to stop churn 2) cordon new nodes with bad drivers 3) increase container restart backoff / init delay to avoid thundering restarts. suggestions?

sam: agree. we should also disable burst policy in the routing layer so new traffic doesn't force huge scaling. I'd also enable a lower-memory model variant for high-concurrency routes as fallback.

devops-bot: deploy request queued by maria: `patch autoscaler --stabilizationWindow=180s && kubectl scale deployment/serving --replicas=40`

emma: incoming handoff in 20m. taking notes: plan = pause autoscaler -> scale to 40 -> drain bad nodes -> verify OOMs stop -> enable fallback model routing -> re-enable autoscaler with stabilization window 3m and max-step 10% once stable.

maria: executing step 1 now: patching autoscaler to paused = true.

sam: pushing a temporary routing rule to prefer quantized model variant for route `/api/generate` for non-enterprise tenants. example rule: `route-pref: model-q3 -> fallback: model-fp16`

talia: surfacing to customers: posting status update to status.redwood.ai — flagging degraded performance for some customers in us-east-1. ETA unknown.

maria: scaled replicas to 40. monitoring.
more_text:
emma: after scale to 40, pod restarts dropped by 70% in 5m, but we still see a handful of OOM on older gpu nodes. suspect driver mismatch on recently replaced nodes.

sam: grep across node logs shows `nvidia-driver 535.54` on new nodes vs `535.66` on older pool. CUDA library mismatch causing some allocations to fail under heavy vram pressure.

jordan: scheduling note: recent node auto-upgrade rolled a subset with older driver; Ill mark the node pool for upgrade. In the short term, we should cordon nodes with older driver and shift traffic.

maria: cordoning nodes with label `driver=535.54` now.

devops-bot: cordon operation completed on 6 nodes.

maria: observed traffic fallback to remaining nodes, memory pressure reduced further.

talia: created support post to affected customers, adding engineering note about mitigation steps and ETA for full resolution.

sam: applying longer container restart backoff: patch deployment `--patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"runtime","livenessProbe":{"failureThreshold":5,"periodSeconds":60}}]}}}}'`

emma: rolling monitoring checks: token-per-second latency, 95th p95 latency, retry rates. Adding an alert to catch any spike >20% relative to baseline.

maria: quick checklist for next phase before re-enabling autoscaler:
- stabilize node pool drivers (upgrade fingerprint)
- validate fallback routes and model variants under load (stress test)
- increase autoscaler stabilizationWindow to 180s and max surge step to 15%
- run a canary with traffic shaping

nate: i'm ondeck at +20m, taking handoff. any blockers?

maria: nothing blocking; ongoing tasks: node upgrades in progress, monitoring green for 10m. handoff docs in incident doc: https://internal/incidents/4291001234 (link). I left the autoscaler paused and replicas pinned to 40.

nate: ack. i'll keep the thread muted but watch metrics and coordinate with support. will escalate if restarts or latency rebounds.

talia: support note: we have 12 enterprise customers impacted; providing credit and near-term mitigation steps. tracking these in JIRA INC-33891.

sam: postmortem action items (tentative):
- autoscaler: add safety throttle and stabilization defaults, fail-closed on malformed config
- runtime: add additional preflight driver check on node join to avoid driver mismatch
- routing: auto-fallback to quantized variants when memory pressure detected
- observability: add a combined signal alerting for "replica-churn + OOMs"

maria: thanks all. incident status: mitigated -> degraded. moving to monitoring. if any regression, reopen pager. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident update: severity lowered to P1 (degraded). next update scheduled in 30m or on-change.
